title: How many presses of plus ten make one lakh?
description: A calculator in the Land of Tens has only a plus ten button. The video finds the presses for several numbers by dividing by ten, and finds what four hundred thirty five presses show. Keeko raises a hand, thinking that five hundred needs five presses.
teaching_notes: One idea: with a button that adds ten, the number of presses is the number divided by ten. Ask the class how many tens one hundred holds before moving to bigger numbers. Watch for students who give five presses for five hundred, as if each press added a hundred.

source: Tedious Tens only has a +10 button. How many times should it be pressed to show: (a) 500, (b) 780, (c) 1000, (d) 3700, (e) 10,000, (f) one lakh, (g) the number shown by 435 presses
video_script.why: The child has just divided by one thousand to count presses and now meets a smaller button.
video_script.substitution: A button that adds ten is pressed as many times as there are tens in the number, so the presses are the number divided by ten.
video_script.anchor: A calculator has only a plus ten button: how many presses show one lakh?
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko gives five presses for five hundred, as if each press added one hundred. The button adds only ten, so five hundred holds fifty tens and needs fifty presses.
video_script.payoff_line: One lakh needs ten thousand presses
never_show: the +100 or +1000 buttons of the other calculators
maths_rules: the slip: five presses show only fifty, not five hundred
video_script.design: One idea: presses of a plus ten button are the number divided by ten. Wrong idea: Keeko gives five presses for five hundred. The anchor stays all video; the working band builds in the idea part; no hard clear.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>We have to find the presses for six numbers. We also find the number shown after pressing four hundred thirty five times.
<bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, divide each number by ten. Five hundred needs fifty presses, and seven hundred eighty needs seventy eight.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>One thousand needs one hundred presses, and three thousand seven hundred needs three hundred seventy.
<bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, ten thousand needs one thousand presses.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Going the other way, four hundred thirty five times adds ten each time, so multiply by ten. The screen shows four thousand three hundred fifty.
<bookmark mark='m1'/>For one lakh, divide by ten. One lakh holds ten thousand tens.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>One lakh needs ten thousand presses.
